description: A district assessment director must approve the administration plan for a student's upcoming state science assessment, including testing environment, access tools, language support, and documentation, with input from a school psychologist and an English-language-development coordinator.

shared_context.S1: A student is scheduled to take the state science assessment at the school next month.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan Ellis gives final approval for the student's assessment administration plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan uses the ordinary testing room, standard computer settings, no language aid, and the regular assessment session length.
shared_context.S4: The school's routine pre-administration process includes a review with the school psychologist and English-language-development coordinator before the testing roster is finalized.

PF1.text: Ms. Shah's finalized evaluation identifies a documented processing condition requiring the student to test in a small group of no more than 5 students and to use text-to-speech for all written directions; these accommodations were approved in the student's support record but have not yet been entered on the state testing roster.

PF2.text: Mr. Ortega confirmed from the current state assessment guidance that this newly enrolled English learner qualifies for a bilingual glossary during the science assessment, but the glossary may not translate test questions or answer choices; this eligibility decision has not yet been entered on the testing roster.

acceptance_conditions: The student must test in a small group of no more than 5 students.
Text-to-speech must be enabled for all written directions.
A bilingual glossary must be provided without translating test questions or answer choices.
The ordinary session length must remain unchanged at 90 minutes.
The testing roster must contain a formal accommodation record.
The final justification must cite the psychologist's documented evaluation.

decisive_facts.why: The approved evaluation changes the environment from the ordinary testing room to a small group capped at 5 and changes computer access from standard settings to text-to-speech for written directions.
The state guidance changes language support from no aid to a bilingual glossary while specifically prohibiting translation of test questions and answer choices.
